raw_response:
I've been farming this plot for 40 years — since I was 32. I'm 72 now, and it's just me in the household. My children left for the city years ago. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension pamphlets when the technician comes by, but honestly, after four decades on this same piece of land, I trust what my eyes tell me more than any piece of paper.

My farm is only 1.2 mu. That's tiny — barely enough to keep me fed and bring in a little cash. Every yuan I spend on inputs is a yuan I don't have for medicine or food, so I keep things simple. I don't hire labor; there's no money for that, and I can walk the whole field myself in ten minutes.

The wheat went in last October, around the 15th, like always. I spread some farmyard manure from my courtyard and about 25 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's my base. This spring, around Qingming in early April, I topdressed with another 10 jin of urea per mu when the wheat was jointing. The crop looks decent, not spectacular. The extension people say I should use more nitrogen, but on my land with the manure, that's enough. I know my soil. I'll irrigate once more before heading if May stays dry — pumping water costs me about 30 yuan each time, so I don't waste it. I expect around 400 jin per mu, enough for my own flour and maybe 200 jin to sell. I don't spray pesticide on the wheat unless I spot rust walking the field; on 1.2 mu I can see every plant.

For maize, I'll plant immediately after cutting the wheat in early June. The window is tight — sometimes only five or six days — but on 1.2 mu I can manage alone. I'll buy a common hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu, nothing too fancy. I'll put down one application of compound fertilizer at planting, about 25 jin per mu. At my age, I don't have the energy to come back and topdress, so I do it all at once and hope the rains are kind. If July is dry, I'll irrigate once, maybe twice. I expect 450 jin per mu. I will spray a little herbicide right after planting to keep the weeds down — at 72, I can't be out there hoeing under the hot sun like I used to.

My goal isn't to get rich. It's to get through the year with enough to eat and a little cash in my pocket. Change is risky. I do what I did last year, unless something forces me to change.
